title: Waltz of the Flowers, in three recordings
work: Waltz of the Flowers — principal-waltz passage
question: Stokowski, Robinson and a concert band play the harp flourish, the horn tune and the waltz that follows.
intro: The harp plays a flourish, and four horns begin the dance. Stokowski’s Philadelphia orchestra and Robinson’s London players keep Tchaikovsky’s scoring, in which the violins then take over. Lawrence Odom’s concert-band arrangement gives the string parts to wind players.

recordings.label: Leopold Stokowski, Philadelphia Orchestra
recordings.note: The Philadelphia Orchestra in Camden’s Trinity Church studio, with the original horn melody and string accompaniment.

recordings.label: Stanford Robinson, National Symphony Orchestra
recordings.note: London’s National Symphony Orchestra plays Tchaikovsky’s scoring, recorded at Kingsway Hall in January 1945.

recordings.label: United States Air Force Band
recordings.note: Lawrence Odom’s arrangement for concert band, recorded for Christmas on Stage and Screen. The wind instruments play the parts written for strings.

passages.label: Horn melody
passages.note: Four horns play the first tune above a plucked bass and quiet chords from the strings.

passages.label: Clarinet runs between horn phrases
passages.note: The clarinet plays runs of quick notes between the horns’ phrases; the accompaniment keeps up the three-beat dance rhythm.

passages.label: String melody
passages.note: The strings play a fuller melody while brass chords mark the beat and the woodwind add quick flourishes.
